output.summary: KEP-576 (Dry-run, sig-api-machinery) is recorded as implemented at stage stable, with status history implemented from 2020-12-30. The discussion shows the KEP was moved to implemented retroactively, after the feature had been declared beta, and that the status change skipped PRR review.
output.rationale: The feature was tracked through release milestones from 1.12 onward, with docs placeholder PRs and a stated plan to "go GA for 1.17". The status was later changed to implemented via PR #2598 and retroactively re-declared at beta by PR #2867, which skipped PRR. Maintainers in PR #3007 debated whether implemented should map to stage stable and added a validation rule for it.

alternatives.option: Keep the KEP at implementable with alpha or beta stage
alternatives.why_not: Sources do not discuss this option; the KEP was instead moved to implemented, per the comments on PR #3007 and PR #2598.
A maintainer argued that perma-beta should be avoided: "we really shouldn't be leaving stuff in a perma-beta state." This was said about a different KEP, not KEP-576.

evidence.quote: is the PR that moved this KEP to implemented. It landed after https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/2672 (which made PRR required for implementable)
This KEP was initially declared implementable at alpha, before PRR was required. The retroactive PR incorrectly called this "implemented" at beta, so it skipped PRR this cycle.
Given that this KEP is related to prow, and not to anything that is contained in a kubernetes release, I think this is pretty uncontroversial
adds an extra validation check for `status:implemented == stage:stable`, it turns out nothing else violates this so I'd rather keep it as a rule
